title: The Rise and Fall of Motivation 2.0
coreMove: Use rewards and rules where the path is clear; for creative work, design for curiosity, contribution, and self-direction.

exampleSpecs.audience: Rowan, a product lead deciding how much control a wiki needs
exampleSpecs.stakes: The team must decide whether a public contribution space needs tighter approval or clearer invitation.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the choice between Encarta-style control and a Wikipedia-style contribution path.

exampleSpecs.audience: Imani, a trainer separating routine work from judgment work
exampleSpecs.stakes: New supervisors are about to apply one factory-style rule to every task.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Taylor as a useful but limited model.

exampleSpecs.audience: Soren, an ethics instructor making fairness visible
exampleSpecs.stakes: A class is tempted to explain every pricing choice as simple self-interest.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the fairness lesson to complicate a pure incentive story.

exampleSpecs.audience: Beatrice, a release lead opening work without losing standards
exampleSpecs.stakes: An open-source team needs more contributors but cannot let quality collapse.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Turn the Wikipedia lesson into a practical contribution design.

exampleSpecs.audience: Keisha, a lab manager reading a short-term productivity jump carefully
exampleSpecs.stakes: A lab gets more logged output after adding check-ins, but curiosity is dropping.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show how the wrong operating system can suppress the behavior it wants.

exampleSpecs.audience: Galen, a support manager redesigning scripts
exampleSpecs.stakes: Agents need consistency without losing the ability to solve unusual customer problems.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply the routine-versus-heuristic diagnosis to a service workflow.
